text.title: AI Prompt as Commit Artefact Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether the commit actually carries an AI-authored hunk, whether a strict message parser sits downstream, and how large the prompt is — to full trailer discipline, by-reference prompt storage, or skip.

decision-tree.root-question: Does this commit contain at least one hunk written or rewritten by a model, as opposed to formatter output, a regenerated lockfile, or a `git revert`?

conclusion.verdict: skip; a trailer on a non-AI commit is a false positive that inflates the audit denominator

branch.question: Does a downstream tool parse commit messages against a closed trailer allowlist (release-please, commitlint) that does not yet list the `Faion-*` keys?

conclusion.verdict: halt; extend the parser's trailer allowlist first, then install enforcement at the `commit-msg` stage before any trailer is written

branch.question: Is the prompt longer than a single line, or does it embed context that a secret scanner would flag (credentials, customer records, PII)?

conclusion.verdict: apply, but commit the scrubbed prompt as `.prompts/<slug>.md` in the same commit and carry only path plus digest in the trailer
apply the full methodology; inline `Faion-*` block as the final paragraph with a dated model id, enforced by the `commit-msg` hook
